summary: Saginaw River range lights on Saginaw Bay: an 1841 stone light replaced in 1876 by rear and front range towers, kept by the Brawn and Burke families, rear light deactivated 1960 or 1963.

corrections.why: The rear range tower and dwelling standing today date from 1876. The 1841 stone light was demolished in 1876 (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: square pyramidal tower built into a two-story dwelling, yellow brick
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends describes the rear light as a square pyramidal tower built into a dwelling corner, of yellow brick.

corrections.proposed: 1963 (LighthouseFriends); 1960 kept in the station record, unreconciled
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the rear tower light was deactivated in 1963 when a new channel was dredged. The station record gives 1960 from Rowlett's directory, not read here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record (1960) and LighthouseFriends (1963) disagree. The Commissioner and Bulletin volumes read here stop before either year. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends dates the electric lights to 1915 (both towers). The Lighthouse Service Bulletin for 1916 lists the range lights among those changed from oil to electric incandescent, and the Commissioner's list for 30 June 1916 shows them as electric. The story gives both dates.
USLHS gives 1841 for the station; LighthouseFriends supports 1841 for the stone light. The 1876 range tower is a different structure.
LighthouseFriends calls Julia head keeper until 1877; the archive roster calls her acting principal keeper from 1873 to 1877. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Julia R. Brawn is also written Julia R. Brawn-Way in the roster and Julia R. Way as assistant; the story uses Julia Brawn for the widow and names the roster's stints. The sources do not say how Nellie Buzzard (first assistant 1883-1886) was related to Edward John Buzzard (head keeper 1883-1886); the story says so. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the nautical-mile conversion was removed because the source gives statute miles; the 1896 plank walk is at printed p. 142 (entry 1303, scan 170); the 1960 roster discontinuance date is no longer tied to the 1963 deactivation. The 1960/1963 deactivation conflict is open. The 1915/1916 electric-lighting conflict is open (both dates are in the text). The 1837-1841 history rests on LighthouseFriends alone (the corpus Board volumes begin in 1891). NRHP nomination 84001373 was not readable (the NPGallery PDF returned no text; the NARA catalog is out of bounds). Commissioner page numbers for 1916, 1917, 1918 and 1919 are read from the corpus OCR index; the 1918 entry (scan 367) falls inside the 'During the Fiscal Year 1918' table of vessels and employees rendering service, and the 1919 entry (scan 462) inside the 1919 'Continued' table; both table headings were checked on the corpus index. The 1896 plank walk is cited to the volume (no page index); entry 1303 is as printed in the OCR. The owner is Dow Chemical per LighthouseFriends; not checked against the owner or the society. Newspaper searches for the range lights and for Burke (Michigan papers, 1900-1925) returned nothing usable.
